checks.a_analysis: I reviewed the output text against the source PDF. All headings, paragraphs, and list items have a direct basis in the source document. No fabricated sections or introductory/conclusory text were found beyond expected AI-generated alt text and table summaries. The weirdly formatted table in section 1.2 is simply a fragmented sentence from the source ('There were no significant deviations reported in the project elements in comparison to the design plans.'), not a fabrication.

I verified all contact information including addresses and phone numbers. The NCDENR address on the cover page matches. Wildlands Engineering addresses (1430 S. Mint St and 5605 Chapel Hill Rd) match. Phone numbers for Wildlands (704-332-7754) and contacts like Daniel Taylor (919.851.9986), Charlie Bruton (919.242.6555), and Kirsten Gimbert (704.332.7754 ext. 110) all match the source exactly.

All pages and sections from the source PDF are represented in the output JSON. The appendices and figures are correctly sequenced and identified. Text content in the executive summary, methodology, and references is present.

Significant row loss was observed in Table 1 and Table 4. Table 1 in the source lists five reaches (A1, A2, B1, B2, B3) in the 'Project Components' section, but the output only shows Reach A1, merged into a single cell. Additionally, Table 1 in the source includes 'Component Summation' and 'BMP Elements' sections which are entirely absent from the output. Table 4 in the source (Project Baseline Information and Attributes) contains over 40 rows of data across multiple categories, but the output JSON represents only 4 rows total. These losses exceed the 20% threshold for materiality. Tables 8a and 8b contain placeholders with '[N elements...]' style text and are excluded from this evaluation per instructions.

checks.a_analysis: The output document was reviewed for duplicated content blocks such as paragraphs or list items appearing multiple times. No instances of structural content duplication were found; the text flow represents the source without repetition of sections.

The heading hierarchy in the output generally follows the source structure. While some level adjustments were made (e.g., subsection 1.2.1 is assigned the same H3 level as 1.2), this falls under acceptable accessibility normalization. There are no skips (e.g., H2 to H4) or illogical nesting.

Significant structural corruption and loss occurred in the conversion of tables. 1) A paragraph on page 5 ('There were no significant deviations...') was incorrectly converted into a 2x2 table in Section 1.2. 2) Table 1 (page 11) is severely truncated, containing only the first row of data and omitting all summation and BMP elements. 3) Table 4 (page 14) is truncated, omitting nearly 90% of the baseline attributes and summary information. 4) Tables 8a and 8b (pages 28-29) were replaced entirely by text strings in brackets (e.g., '[Table 8a...]'), resulting in total loss of the complex matrix structure and data.
checks.b_evidence_source: Multiple tables across pages 5, 11, 14, 28, and 29 containing multi-row and multi-column project data.
checks.b_evidence_output: Truncated tables in section 9 (Tables 1 and 4) and placeholder strings replacing tables in section 15 (Tables 8a and 8b).

checks.a_analysis: The HTML document generally follows the visual organization of the source PDF. It maintains the hierarchical structure of sections, preserves the placement of images relative to text, and includes a functional table of contents. While the layout is simplified for web viewing (single-column responsive design), the overall visual flow is consistent with the source's intent.

Several major table rendering issues were identified. 1) Table 1 (Project Components and Mitigation Credits) has lost its nested header structure (specifically the 'R' and 'RE' sub-categories for Stream and Wetland types), making the data columns ambiguous. 2) In section 1.2, a plain text sentence has been incorrectly converted into a table format ('Project Element Deviations Summary'), with the sentence fragmented across cells, which disrupts the reading flow. 3) Tables 8a and 8b are structurally broken: the HTML table header row has 10 columns while the data rows contain 13 values, leading to header-data misalignment. Furthermore, the critical 'P' (Planted) and 'T' (Total) sub-headers are missing, making the data uninterpretable.
checks.b_evidence_source: Table 1 headers with R/RE sub-columns (page 11); 'There were no significant deviations reported...' text (page 5); Tables 8a and 8b with 17 columns including P/T sub-headers (pages 28-29).
checks.b_evidence_output: Table 1 with flattened headers; 'Project Element Deviations Summary' table in Section 1.2; Tables 8a and 8b with column count mismatch and missing P/T sub-headers.
checks.b_evidence_location: Table 1 (Project Components and Mitigation Credits), Section 1.2 (Project Element Deviations Summary), and Appendix 2 (Tables 8a and 8b).

checks.a_analysis: All meaningful images from the source PDF are correctly rendered in the HTML. This includes the cover photograph, the site logos, the location and asset maps (Figures 1-3), and the full set of 16 vegetation plot photographs in Appendix 2. No broken image icons were observed.

The content blocks in the HTML output correspond 1:1 with the sections and elements of the source PDF. There are no instances of paragraphs, tables, or sections being visually duplicated within the converted document.
